transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that made you decide to come in today?

My mood has been all over the place—either way too high and wired or snapping at people over nothing. I feel like I’m constantly “on,” full of energy, can’t slow down or sit still, and it’s starting to mess things up at work and with my family.

When you feel this way, do you ever have sudden attacks of intense fear or discomfort that peak within minutes—with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest tightness, or feeling like you might die or lose control—or is it more of a constant, ongoing state of being keyed up and wired most of the time?
It’s more of a constant, ongoing wired feeling, like I’m revved up all the time and can’t switch off. I don’t really get those sudden, out‑of‑the-blue fear attacks where I feel like I’m about to die.
Have you also had periods lasting at least two weeks where you felt mostly down or depressed, with low energy and loss of interest in things, that were clearly different from these “revved up” times?
I’m not really sure I’ve had a full two weeks like that. I’ll have a day or two where I crash and feel kind of flat or tired, but it usually swings back into the revved‑up mode pretty quickly.

During your “revved up” times, do you ever feel so unusually confident, talkative, or driven to do things (like spending, risky sex, big projects) that other people say you’re not yourself or you get into serious trouble at work, with money, or in relationships?

Yeah, when I’m like that I feel unstoppable, like everything I touch will work out, and I talk a mile a minute. I start a bunch of projects, make big plans, and I’ve spent more money than I should; my family keeps saying I’m “over the top” and my boss has warned me I’m being too intense at work.

During your highest, most ‘unstoppable’ times, have you ever had experiences like believing you had special powers or a special mission, or hearing or seeing things others couldn’t, or needing almost no sleep for several days without feeling tired?

Yeah, when I’m at my highest I feel like I’m on some kind of special mission, like I’m meant to do something huge and that I have abilities other people don’t. I’ve gone several nights on just an hour or two of sleep and still felt totally wired, and I’ve also heard voices or seen things that other people around me didn’t seem to notice, but only when I’m in that really “up” state.

Before this current period of feeling revved up and on a special mission, have you ever had a separate episode in your life where your mood was unusually high or irritable for several days or longer, even if you weren’t feeling this extreme or having voices or visions?

Yeah, I’ve had a few stretches like that before, just not as intense as this one. Maybe a week or so at a time where I was extra upbeat or snappy, sleeping less, talking more, taking on a lot of things at once, but it never got to the point of hearing or seeing things back then.

At any point in your life—separate from these high, wired times—have you ever had a stretch of at least two weeks where you felt mostly depressed or empty nearly every day, with low energy and loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t think I’ve ever had a solid two weeks like that. I’ll have brief dips where I feel tired or a bit down, but they don’t last very long before I swing back into the more wired, high mode.

Thinking about your current and past “revved up” or unstoppable periods, what is the longest one has lasted without clearly returning to your usual, more normal mood—would you say it went on for at least a week straight?

Yeah, this current one has definitely gone on way longer than a week. It’s been pretty much continuous, or at least mostly there, for many months now without really going back to what I’d call my normal mood.

Before this long high, wired period started, did you ever have a time in your life—separate from any “up” or wired mood—when you felt clearly depressed or very down for at least two weeks in a row, even if it was many years ago?

I’m not really sure I’ve ever had a full two weeks like that. I remember some rough patches where I felt low and unmotivated for a few days at a time, but nothing that stands out as a long, solid stretch of being really down.

Before this long high, wired period began, had you recently started or increased any medications, drugs, or alcohol (including antidepressants, stimulants, or street drugs), or has this mood change happened completely on its own without any clear trigger like that?

No, nothing really changed with meds or substances before this started. I wasn’t on any new prescriptions or upping anything, and I don’t use drugs and only drink occasionally, so as far as I can tell it just kind of kicked in on its own.

(3) Across the entire history, the patient denies any clearly separate, sustained (≥2 weeks) depressive episode. Because there are multiple distinct elevated‑mood episodes over time, a recurrent mood‑episode disorder with current severe elevated episode and psychotic symptoms must now be considered in addition to a single severe episode diagnosis. We therefore add a recurrent mood‑episode code as a second candidate, while retaining the original single‑episode severe elevated‑mood diagnosis as still plausible, since it is not yet fully clear whether the prior briefer high periods met full syndromal criteria or duration for separate episodes. Further questioning is needed to clarify the exact number, duration, and functional impact of past high episodes, so the candidate list is expanded to [F30.2, F31.2] and is_final remains false.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation only. No previous candidate list was provided, so this is the first differential set. The patient reports markedly elevated/"too high" mood, high energy, decreased ability to slow down or sit still, and irritability that is impairing work and family functioning. This pattern raises concern for an episodic mood disorder with possible elevated mood, so a bipolar-spectrum condition (unspecified at this stage) is the leading consideration (coded here as F31.9, unspecified episode/severity, pending clarification of duration, associated symptoms, and any history of depression or psychosis). However, without details on duration, sleep, grandiosity, risk-taking, or functional consequences, it is premature to narrow specifically within bipolar diagnoses. Anxiety-related conditions (F41.1 generalized anxiety, F41.0 panic) remain in the differential because patients often describe being "on" and restless, though the description of "way too high" mood and snapping at others leans more toward mood dysregulation than pure anxiety. A depressive disorder (F32.9) is included because many patients present in an elevated or irritable phase but also have a history of low mood episodes that has not yet been explored. No conditions have been ruled out yet; this is an initial broad list that will be refined with further history (sleep, duration, cycling pattern, substance use, psychotic symptoms, and past episodes).

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets full criteria for a manic episode with psychotic symptoms (elevated/irritable mood, markedly increased energy and activity, decreased need for sleep, grandiosity, pressured speech, risky spending and overinvolvement in projects, and mood‑congruent psychotic features) lasting well over a week and causing clear functional impairment. There is no history of a distinct major depressive episode lasting at least two weeks at any point in life, so criteria for bipolar affective disorder, current episode manic with psychotic symptoms (F31.2), which requires at least one past affective episode (typically depressive or hypomanic/mania separated by euthymia), are not clearly fulfilled. Given the available history, a single manic episode with psychotic symptoms (F30.2) is the most accurate current diagnosis, with bipolar disorder remaining a strong longitudinal consideration.
